paragraphs.title: The Water Flowing from the Temple

answers: From under the threshold of the house
easy.explanation: The waters issued from under the threshold of the house.
easy.q: From where did the waters issue?

easy.explanation: The waters flowed eastward from the house.
easy.q: In which direction did the waters flow?

easy.explanation: The waters increased from shallow water to a river that could not be crossed.
easy.q: What happened to the waters as they were measured?

answers: The waters were to the ankles
The waters were to the loins
The waters were deep enough to swim in
medium.explanation: After the first thousand cubits, the waters were to the ankles.
medium.q: What was the first depth measured?

medium.explanation: The KJV says the first measured depth reached the ancles, or ankles.
medium.q: What does “the waters were to the ancles” mean?

answers: The waters had risen and were too deep
medium.explanation: The waters had risen so that the river could not be passed over.
medium.q: Why could Ezekiel not pass over the river at the final measurement?

answers: The waters flowed in a circle
The waters grew deeper in stages
The waters remained at the same depth
challenge.explanation: Each measurement revealed a greater depth, showing a gradual increase.
challenge.q: What does the repeated measuring of a thousand cubits show?

answers: The house was the source of the river
The waters came only from the sea
The river began in the desert
challenge.explanation: The waters originated beneath the house, making it the source of the flow.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the waters coming from under the threshold of the house?

answers: Loins, ankles, then an uncrossable river
Ankles, knees, loins, then an uncrossable river
An uncrossable river, knees, then ankles
challenge.explanation: The passage gives the order as ankles, knees, loins, and finally a river too deep to cross.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly gives the increasing depths?

paragraphs.title: Healing the Dead Sea and Blessing Life

easy.explanation: There were very many trees on both sides of the river.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel see beside the river?

easy.explanation: The waters entering the sea would be healed.
easy.q: What would happen to the waters when they reached the sea?

easy.explanation: The passage says the fishers would spread forth nets.
easy.q: What would the fishers do along the river?

answers: Fish would multiply and living things would flourish
medium.explanation: The healed waters would support a great multitude of fish and other living things.
medium.q: What would result when the waters came into the sea?

answers: A place for fishermen to use their nets
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a place where fishers could spread their nets.
medium.q: What does “a place to spread forth nets” describe?

answers: They bore fruit and leaves for medicine
medium.explanation: Their fruit was for meat, and their leaves were for medicine.
medium.q: What was special about the trees beside the river?

answers: The miry places and marishes that remained salty
challenge.explanation: The miry places and marishes were not healed and were given to salt.
challenge.q: What detail contrasts with the blessing of life in the river?

answers: The waters from the sanctuary sustain the trees
The trees dry up the river
The fruit prevents the fish from multiplying
challenge.explanation: The trees receive life-giving waters that issued out of the sanctuary.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the river waters and the trees?

answers: The waters could not support life
The river became a source of abundance and life
The fish lived only in salty marshes
challenge.explanation: The fish and fishers show the abundance produced by the healed waters.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the many fishers and the exceeding many fish?

paragraphs.title: The Boundaries of the Future Land

easy.explanation: The land was to be inherited according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
easy.q: For whom was the land to be inherited?

easy.explanation: The Lord said that Joseph would have two portions.
easy.q: Which tribe was to receive two portions?

easy.explanation: The passage describes all four sides of the land.
easy.q: In which directions are the boundaries described?

medium.explanation: The great sea formed the west side.
medium.q: What was the western boundary of the land?

answers: Joseph would rule over the entire land
medium.explanation: Joseph was assigned two portions in the inheritance.
medium.q: What does “Joseph shall have two portions” mean?

medium.explanation: The eastern boundary was described from the land of Israel by Jordan toward the east sea.
medium.q: What body of water is mentioned in the eastern boundary?

answers: The boundary concerned only the coast
The eastern boundary extended into lands east of Jordan
The eastern boundary was not described
challenge.explanation: These places occur in the description of the eastern side, including territory beyond Jordan.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from the mention of Hauran, Damascus, and Gilead on the east side?

answers: To define the land on every side
To describe only the river’s course
To show that the land was not divided
challenge.explanation: The four directional descriptions establish the extent of the land.
challenge.q: Why is it important that all four sides are described?

answers: Joseph was excluded from the inheritance
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically states that Joseph would have two portions.
challenge.q: What was Joseph’s role in the division of the land?

paragraphs.title: Division of the Land and Inclusion of Resident Foreigners

easy.explanation: The land was to be divided according to the tribes of Israel.
easy.q: Among whom was the land to be divided?

answers: People who lived only by the sea
easy.explanation: The strangers living among Israel would receive an inheritance.
easy.q: Who else would receive an inheritance?

answers: In a tribe chosen from far away
In the tribe where he sojourned
In a separate tribe of his own
easy.explanation: The stranger would receive an inheritance in the tribe where he lived.
easy.q: In which tribe would a stranger receive his inheritance?

answers: They were regarded as part of the community
They had to leave the land
They could not receive an inheritance
medium.explanation: The passage gives them standing among the children of Israel and an inheritance.
medium.q: What is the significance of treating the strangers as born in the country among Israel?

answers: Within the inheritance assigned among Israel’s tribes
medium.explanation: The strangers were included within the tribal division of the land.
medium.q: What does “among the tribes of Israel” mean in this context?

answers: The tribe in which he sojourned
The number of fish in the river
medium.explanation: The stranger received his inheritance in the tribe where he lived.
medium.q: What determined where a stranger received his inheritance?

answers: They received an inheritance within the existing tribes
challenge.explanation: They were included within the tribe among which they lived rather than separated into their own group.
challenge.q: How did the treatment of the strangers differ from establishing a separate group?

answers: He had settled and lived among the community
He was required to be a fisherman
challenge.explanation: The wording describes a resident foreigner whose family had become established among Israel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the stranger begetting children among Israel?

answers: Inheritance was given only according to ancestry
Resident strangers among Israel shared in the land
A person’s place of residence had no importance
challenge.explanation: The passage includes resident strangers in the inheritance according to the tribe where they lived.
challenge.q: What principle emerges from including strangers in the tribal inheritance?
